instruction: Design the main screen (a single page) for an in-game friends and party system. Include a player profile header, searchable friends list with avatars and online states, pending requests, a selected-friend detail panel, and clear Add Friend, Invite to Game, and Battle actions. Show at least one active party or invitation state. Put strong emphasis on social clarity, status legibility, warm personality, coherent component design, and polished game-interface finish.

history.critique: Strong warm ember identity and a complete three-column social layout, but real gaps remain. Brief & Intent: (1) Pending requests are only implied by the 'Requests 3' tab and the bell badge — no actual request rows with Accept/Decline are visible, so a required element is effectively omitted from the screen; (2) the 'Emberfall Party ACTIVE' card is clipped at the viewport bottom, so the required active-party/invitation state (member slots, ready states, invite/leave controls) is only half shown; (3) action logic contradicts state — 'Add Friend' sits on the player's OWN profile, and the selected friend Emberlyn (already a friend and already in your party) is offered 'Add' and 'Invite', both invalid for her. Clarity & Hierarchy: two high-saturation gradient primaries (gold 'Add Friend' left, orange 'Challenge to Battle' right) split focal priority; status dots conflate two dimensions — green means online, in-party, AND browsing, which directly undermines the brief's 'status legibility' goal; the small top-right glyph+number on each row and the inconsistent '+' avatar badge are unlabeled affordances; the left profile's stat tiles duplicate the detail panel, making three columns compete for focus. Visual System & Craft: the hand-drawn scribble ring around the main avatar reads as an unfinished placeholder rather than polished game UI; a stray gray dot artifact overlaps the right-panel avatar; 'Rank Platinum II' wraps awkwardly and 'Invite to Game' wraps to two uneven lines; the clipped party card is layout jank. Expressiveness: the Emberhall/Emberfall naming and warm palette give genuine personality, but the placeholder ring, clipped card, and fairly generic three-column grid undercut the 'polished game-interface finish' the brief demands. Key trade-offs: fitting requests plus a full party card on one screen vs density (resolve with a compact request strip and a full-width party footer rather than a tall left card); a globally clear 'Add Friend' vs contextual correctness (keep one Add entry point and make detail actions state-aware); status richness vs legibility (split availability from party membership instead of overloading dot color).
history.suggestion: 1) Restore omitted content first: add a compact 'Requests' strip (three horizontal chips: avatar, name, mutual-friends count, Accept/Decline) directly above the friends list so pending requests are visible without a tab switch; move the active party into a full-width footer bar (or the bottom of the left column) that fits the viewport and shows 4/5 slots with one empty 'Invite' slot to make the invitation state explicit. 2) Fix action/state logic: rename the left profile button to 'Find Friends' (or move Add Friend to the top bar as the single global Add entry point); in the friend detail, since Emberlyn is already a friend in your party, replace 'Add' with 'Message' and replace 'Invite' with a state-aware 'Ready Up' (or a disabled 'In Party'), keeping 'Challenge to Battle' as the only primary gradient CTA — demote the left button to an outline secondary. 3) Unify the status system: dot = availability only (green online, amber away, red in battle, blue matchmaking); show party membership with a gold ring or small party icon plus the 'Emberfall Party' label; make 'Browsing' read as online-plus-activity rather than a separate green, and add a one-line legend or consistent icon set. 4) Craft pass: replace the scribble ring with a clean forged-gold ring carrying the level notch; delete the stray gray dot on the right avatar; fix the 'Platinum II' wrap and the two-line 'Invite to Game' label; label or remove the row's top-right glyph (e.g., 'played together' with a tooltip) and make the '+' badge a consistent quick-invite affordance with a tooltip, shown only on non-party friends. 5) Hierarchy & expression: trim the left profile to identity + rank + party state + one key stat so the center list and right detail become the clear focal flow; add subtle forged-edge notches and a faint ember glow on the active party card to turn it into the memorable moment, preserving the warm Emberhall identity while reaching production polish — all with inline CSS/SVG, no external libraries or assets.

history.critique: BRIEF & INTENT: Two required elements are under-delivered. (1) 'Pending requests' has no labeled surface — the only evidence is the bell's '3' badge and an unlabeled horizontal strip of mini-cards (Fable, Grim, +a clipped 'S') carrying cryptic ✓/✕ buttons that *imply* accept/decline but are never named; a viewer cannot confirm this is the requests queue. (2) 'Add Friend' is not a clear action: the left CTA reads 'Find Friends' (duplicated in the top bar), and the tiny '+' badges on avatars are ambiguous (invite-to-party vs add). The active-party state IS present (Emberfall 4/5, In Party pills) but is scattered as text labels rather than shown as a roster, and the implied open 5th slot has no 'invite to fill' affordance. CLARITY & HIERARCHY: The middle column stacks two unexplained structures — an unlabeled mini-card strip above the main list — so the eye can't tell what the strip is for; the third card is hard-clipped at the panel's right edge with no scroll cue. The legend row conflates status dots (Online/Away/In Battle/Matchmaking) with action chips ('+ Party', '+ Quick-invite'), muddying status legibility. Avatar badges double-encode state (status dot bottom-right + '+' bottom-left) with no key. Redundancy: 'Find Friends' appears twice, and the top-right user chip repeats the left header's name/party. A large dead zone sits under the left card, unbalancing the grid. VISUAL SYSTEM & CRAFT: The clipped 'S' card is genuine jank; the left avatar's level '42' tab and double ring sit awkwardly on the avatar edge; legend-to-search spacing is cramped; otherwise the ember palette, serif display type, and consistent pills are coherent and production-grade. EXPRESSIVENESS: The forge/ember identity (Emberhall, Pyromancer, Emberforge) is good and content-specific, but the component language is a generic dark dashboard — rounded cards, pills, list rows — with no authored 'moment'; the orphaned mini-card strip reads as an afterthought rather than a designed feature, and the empty bottom-left wastes a chance for a signature party card. TRADE-OFFS: Surfacing requests and a party roster adds density to an already full 3-column layout; the strip's ✓/✕ are the cheapest way to satisfy 'pending requests' if labeled, but a true roster card is needed to fill dead space and make the 4/5 state legible — both can coexist if the strip becomes a compact labeled row and the roster moves to the left column. Making 'Add Friend' explicit competes with the redundant 'Find Friends'; resolving it means sacrificing one duplicate rather than adding a fourth button.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan (self-contained HTML/CSS only, no external assets): P0 — (a) Relabel the clipped mini-card strip as a 'Requests · 3' row, give it a horizontal scroll or 2-up grid so no card clips, and add micro-labels under ✓/✕ ('Accept'/'Decline'); tie the top-bar bell '3' to it visually. (b) Fill the dead bottom-left with an 'Emberfall Party' roster card: 4 member chips + an empty 5th slot with a dashed 'Invite to fill' button and a 4/5 ready progress ring — this makes the active-party state concrete and balances the grid. P1 — (c) Make the three named actions unambiguous: keep 'Find Friends' only in the top bar, change the left primary CTA to 'Add Friend' (keep 'Invite to Game' secondary), and keep 'Challenge to Battle' as the detail-panel primary; (d) split the legend into a status-only dot row and a separate action-chip row, and add a legend key for the avatar '+' = 'Invite to party' so the badge stops reading as 'add friend'. P2 — (e) Remove the duplicate top-right user chip's party text (keep name + level only) to cut redundancy; (f) tighten legend/search spacing and re-seat the level tab off the avatar edge; (g) add one authored moment — a soft ember-glow pulse on the 'ready' party card and a subtle animated ring on the 4/5 progress — to push past generic dashboard styling while preserving the warm identity.
